subject: Re: Redwood vs hyperscaler reliability & SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood call recap + proposed reliability tests

Hi Emily / Acme ML team,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the straightforward context on your latency and availability requirements. Quick recap of the discussion and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

Call highlights:
- Goal: replace part of your inference fleet with a lower-cost, predictable service while meeting strict uptime and error-budget constraints for customer-facing features.
- Key metrics you care about: P95 latency (text gen) <=150ms, sustained throughput up to 100 RPS per model, and an error budget <0.1% for production traffic.
- Hyperscaler baseline: you noted 99.95% historical uptime during spike tests but observed soft failures and throttling during large bursts.
- Differentiators we discussed: Redwood’s dedicated routing + automatic fallback to smaller model variants, prefix KV caching to reduce tail latency, and transparent token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

Proposed next tests (we can run these on the sandbox account):
1) 48-hour soak at 50 RPS (90% gen, 10% embed) to measure error rates and degradation patterns.
2) Burst test: 5-minute spike to 250 RPS to observe throttling/failover behavior and cold-start characteristics.
3) Latency SLO validation: P50/P95/P99 under a realistic request size distribution (we'll use the sample prompt set you shared).

Deliverables from our side:
- SLO comparison report (attached) summarizing Redwood vs. Hyperscaler baseline on uptime, error budget, rate limit behavior, and failover.
- Test harness and load plan in a shared Drive.
- Draft MPA (attached) that outlines mutual responsibilities, ramp schedule, and success criteria.

Ask: can you confirm the sandbox credentials we used during the call are good for the tests, and whether you want us to run the 48-hour soak starting Monday (Mar 15) or earlier?

Thanks — looking forward to validating the reliability profile.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: 20260310-redwood-slo-comparison.pdf (summary, 5 pages)
Attachment: ACME-MPA-draft-20260312.pdf (mutual performance agreement draft)

From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood call recap + proposed reliability tests

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we green-light the soak: 

1) Error budget: when you say <0.1%, is that per-minute errors over the test window or aggregated over each 24h period? We need per-day guarantees for the pilot.
2) During the burst test, can Redwood simulate the same client IP distribution as our prod traffic? Our upstream load balancer sometimes masks retry patterns which are important for failover behavior.
3) Can you also include your observability hooks (trace IDs and token-level latency metrics) in the report so our SREs can correlate with our logs?

Sandbox creds: yes, the sandbox account you used is live for testing. We prefer the soak start on Monday, Mar 15.

Also please add Ben and Marissa to any internal notes — Ben is coordinating procurement and Marissa will own technical sign-off.

—Emily
Emily Turner
Head of ML Platform | Acme Corp
emily.turner@acme.com
